detail.longDescription:
Productive day! 

The backstory is that my existing homelab architecture is as follows: 
- 3x physical nodes running a Proxmox cluster
- 3x #Fedora CoreOS VM's running as #k3s  control plane nodes
- 6x Fedora CoreOS VM's running as k3s worker nodes
- 1x NAS connected via NFS as the storage 

The original goal was to provide layered backups and snapshots for my "mini-prod" for family services. 

In reality, I've realized that having the workload volumes live on the #NAS (which itself gets backed up offsite) is a sufficient backup, since the entire k3s cluster is effectively "cattle."

The overhead of the hypervisor and VM's was pretty substantial, and since it wasn't actually contributing much to resilience, I began questioning the architecture.

So, I made the choice recently to migrate over to #talos, where I'll run a straight up #kubernetes cluster on bare metal. Today was the backup/snapshot, and creation of the first node in the cluster.

I can't do a full, proper comparison yet, since I'm still working on the other nodes....but even just with initial testing, I'm very conservatively getting something like ~40% improvement in performance.
